gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on the VIOFO A329S only the HK6 hardwire kit turns on the camera's own cut-off voltage. That setting protects the car battery during parking recording. The HK4 kit starts automatic parking mode but cannot do this.
standout_why: I compared against Product Bible (cited in both chats), Digital Camera World's A329S 3CH review (cited in chat 2), Notebookcheck's N4 Pro S review and DashCamTalk's N4 Pro S test thread. Car and Driver's tested list was cited in chat 1 but could not be fetched, so I could not check it. ChatGPT already told the shopper that all three picks 'require an appropriate hardwire kit'. Digital Camera World already says the A329S front camera runs 4K at 30 fps, and 60 fps only when the interior camera isn't in use. Product Bible lists the A329S front as '4K, 30fps (front, 3-channel version)' and notes the HK6-F kit only for VIOFO's T330. None of these pages says that A329S battery protection depends on the HK6 kit rather than the HK4. None of them gives the N4 Pro S's per-channel bitrates with all three cameras recording either. The main fact that decides whether a 3-channel plan works (frame rate drops when the cabin camera is added) is already on a page ChatGPT cited, so my angle adds only part of a new fact.
decides: This confirms the pick and does not change it. With all three cameras recording, the VIOFO A329S 3CH and the Vantrue N4 Pro S both record the front at 4K 30 fps. The A329S's 4K 60 fps mode, the headline on its 1CH and 2CH listings, is lost once the cabin camera is in use. The 60 fps mode is therefore not a reason to pay the A329S's higher price for a 3-channel setup, which helps the N4 Pro S as the value pick. Both cameras use a supercapacitor or have no battery, so 24/7 parking recording needs a hardwire kit bought separately. An A329S buyer who wants the camera to protect the car battery should budget for the HK6 kit, not the HK4.
candidates: Vantrue Nexus 4 Pro S (N4 Pro S)
